Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Before implementing a new function, read the existing module and its money/rounding helpers (e.g. ZERO, to_money, round_money) and reuse them so new code matches the project's established Decimal and rounding conventions.
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: For weighted-average or division logic, guard against a zero denominator (e.g. empty lines / total quantity of zero) and return the module's zero constant rather than dividing by zero.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When summing Decimal values, pass an explicit start value (e.g. sum(..., ZERO)) instead of relying on the default int 0, to keep types consistent and avoid mixing int and Decimal.

item.content: When validating an integer parameter, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since bool is a subclass of int and True/False would otherwise pass as 1/0.

Mirror existing error codes and message formats from sibling modules (e.g. reuse 'invalid_state' with the same f-string as issue_invoice/payments) so new validation is consistent with the project's BillingError conventions.

Don't assume to_money/round_money accepts arbitrary input silently; verify how it handles floats, NaN, and non-Decimal types, and rely on its existing error (e.g. 'float_amount') rather than duplicating type checks.
